The optimal tip-speed ratio ranged from 2.3 to 3.6, with the highest values for low c/R and the lowest for high c/R.
Increasing toe-out preset pitch (more negative α ) at constant c/R caused lower performance in the upstream and higher performance downstream.
Increasing net camber, either through virtual or geometric camber, resulted in increased upstream peak performance but reduced performance downstream.

The optimal preset pitch at a given c/R or camber was largely determined by the corresponding virtual incidence, with the optimal performance occurring at a relatively constant net incidence of 0° to +1°.
The authors calculated the chord-based Reynolds number, Re , and noted that the datasets were not in a Reynolds number independent regime.
The virtual camber and virtual incidence concepts, derived from the curved blade trajectory, are key to understanding the aerodynamic behavior and performance of cross-flow turbines.
The main objective is to analyze the individual and combined impacts of c/R, airfoil camber, and preset pitch on cross-flow turbine performance.

The two experimental datasets used are: (1) performance data for turbines with symmetric NACA 0018 blades and various c/R, α , and blade count, and (2) performance data for turbines with ±2% cambered NACA 0018 blades and various α .
The authors propose using net camber and net incidence as effective parameters to understand turbine performance and design behavior.

The authors found that all of the geometric parameters (c/R, camber, and preset pitch) exhibit similar effects on turbine performance and should be considered in conjunction during the design and optimization of turbine geometry.
The authors note that the effects of Reynolds number and blockage are expected to be secondary compared to the geometric parameter effects.
